Before joining the NBA, he played college basketball for the [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin Badgers]], where he became its all-time leading scorer with a total of 2,217 points. From 2007 to 2017, Tucker had a 10-year career in professional basketball, which included playing for the [[Phoenix Suns]] and [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for three years in the NBA. His last team was the [[Hapoel Eilat B.C.|Hapoel Eilat]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]] in 2017, before going into retirement. In 2019, he became the interim assistant coach for his alma mater's men's basketball team at the University of Wisconsin, a position he held until April 2021. ==High school career== Tucker attended [[Lockport Township High School]] in [[Lockport, Illinois]].{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/t/tuckeal02.html|title= Alando Forest Tucker|publisher= Basketball-Reference.Com |access-date= October 30, 2012}} He averaged 21.6 points and seven rebounds per game as a junior. He was one of only two juniors to be named to the ''Herald News'' AA all-area team. As a senior Tucker earned all-state honors averaging 22.2 points while hauling in 7.7 rebounds and dishing 5.7 assists per game. He scored 35 points against Joliet Township, the number one ranked team in the state. After seeing drugs and gang violence from up close throughout his childhood, Tucker and his older brother Antonio made a pact to stay clean and away from substances such as drug, tobacco, and alcohol, as well as tattoos. ==Collegiate career== Tucker started off his [[college basketball]] career in 2002–03 starting 27 of 32 games as a [[freshman]]. He averaged 12.0 points and 5.9 rebounds per game, which helped the Badgers achieve 24 wins, a Big Ten title, and a Sweet 16 at the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]] during that season. In 2003–04, Tucker played in just four games because of a right foot injury. He applied for and received a [[medical redshirt]] after the season. During the 2004–05 season, Tucker started 30 out of 31 games. He led the Badgers in scoring with 15.2 points. He also averaged 6.1 rebounds. At the end of the 2006–07 regular season, Tucker averaged 19.9 points, 5.4 rebounds and 2.0 assists. For the [[2006–07 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|2006–07 season]], Tucker and the Badgers achieved 30 wins and earned their first ever #1 AP ranking in the school's history. On February 10, 2007, Tucker reached the 2,000-point mark in his collegiate career in a game against Iowa. He was the second Wisconsin Badger to ever accomplish this, after [[Michael Finley]].{{cite web|author =Kohl Center, Madison, WI |url=http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=270410275 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090226193902/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=270410275 |url-status=dead |archive-date=February 26, 2009 |title=Tucker hits 2,000-point milestone as Badgers beat Iowa |publisher=ESPN |date=February 10, 2007 |access-date=November 30, 2011}} On March 10, 2007, Tucker broke the all-time [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|Wisconsin]] scoring record (2,147 points) previously held by Michael Finley.{{cite web|author =United Center, Chicago, IL |url=http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=270690275 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120715112717/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=270690275 |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 15, 2012 |title=Tucker breaks scoring mark, leads Badgers past Illini |publisher=ESPN |date=March 10, 2007 |access-date=November 30, 2011}} During this time, he also broke Finley's UW vertical jump record. Tucker's collegiate career ended on March 18, 2007, when the Badgers lost to the [[UNLV]] Runnin' Rebels 74–68 in the second round of the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]]. Tucker finished with 17 points on 4–11 shooting from the field and 8–13 from the line. He also had seven rebounds. In his final season, he was named Big Ten Player of the Year, an NCAA 1st Team All-American, and received Lowe's Senior CLASS Award.{{cite web|author =United Center, Chicago, IL |url=http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=274000059 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070329111045/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=274000059 |url-status=dead |archive-date=March 29, 2007 |title=Coach's son Kruger makes dad proud, leads UNLV to Sweet 16 |publisher=ESPN |date=March 18, 2007 |access-date=November 30, 2011}} He also set school marks at the time for games played (134), starts (126), minutes played (4,297), field goals (798), free throws (520), free throw attempts (817), offensive rebounds (769), and overall points scored (2,217).{{Cite web |title=Alando Tucker {{!}} Director of Student-Athlete Engagement {{!}} Staff Directory |url=https://uwbadgers.com/staff-directory/alando-tucker/650 |access-date=2022-10-26 |website=Wisconsin Badgers |language=en}} Tucker graduated from the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] on May 19, 2007, with a bachelor's degree in Life Sciences Communication. In 2018, he was inducted to UW Athletic's Hall of Fame for his accomplishments in basketball.{{Cite web |title=Alando Tucker (2018) {{!}} UW Athletic Hall of Fame |url=https://uwbadgers.com/honors/university-of-wisconsin-athletic-hall-of-fame/alando-tucker/226 |access-date=2022-10-26 |website=Wisconsin Badgers |language=en}} ==Pro career== ===NBA career=== athletes and staff.{{Cite web |title=Alando Tucker {{!}} Director of Student-Athlete Engagement {{!}} Staff Directory |url=https://uwbadgers.com/staff-directory/alando-tucker/650 |access-date=2022-10-26 |website=Wisconsin Badgers |language=en}} After two years in this role, on July 31, 2019, he was announced as interim assistant coach on for the Badgers for the 2019–20 season.{{Cite web |title=Alando Tucker {{!}} Men's Basketball Coach |url=https://uwbadgers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/coaches/alando-tucker/1501 |access-date=2022-10-26 |website=Wisconsin accident that left him with serious injuries.{{cite web |url= https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/27296588/badgers-all-leading-scorer-tucker-joins-staff|title= Badgers' all-time leading scorer Tucker joins staff|author=|date= July 31, 2019|publisher= ESPN|access-date= August 4, 2021}} Tucker was known for his ability to develop close relationships with the players, which led him to remain as interim assistant coach throughout the 2020–21 season, enjoying popularity among players and fans alike. Following the conclusion of the 2020–21 season, Tucker applied to become a full-time assistant coach, but Wisconsin officials decided to part ways with him. Allegations surfaced in local media surrounding Tucker's desire to take over the head coaching job,{{cite web |last=Potrykus |first=Jeff |date=August 2, 2021 |title=A perfect marriage fails: Alando Tucker could have stayed at UW for years, but his desire to take over as head coach led to his demise |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/uw/2021/08/02/alando-tucker-tried-undermine-greg-gard-and-take-over-uw-coach-wisconsin-badgers/5456411001/ |access-date=August 4, 2021 |publisher=Milwaukee Journal Sentinel}} but he later dismissed these as rumors and denied any accusations of wrongdoing.{{cite web |last=Polzin |first=Jim |date=August 5, 2021 |title=Former UW basketball star, coach Alando Tucker laments 'mistaken assumptions' in first statement since departure |url=https://madison.com/wsj/sports/college/basketball/men/former-uw-basketball-star-coach-alando-tucker-laments-mistaken-assumptions-in-first-statement-since-departure/article_348f84a8-faf2-5b65-bc7d-fbc83e311aef.html |access-date=August 7, 2021 |website=Madison.com |publisher=Wisconsin State Journal}} He finished his 2-year stint with a Big Ten Conference Championship for the 2019 regular season and a 39–23 record. == Personal life == During his stint at Hapoel Tel Aviv, Tucker partnered with an Israeli “Hoops for Kids International” non-for-profit organization for speaking engagements, basketball clinics, and mentorship to impoverished children throughout the Middle East.{{Cite web |title=PLAYER ROSTER |url=https://www.hoopsforkidsintl.org/p |access-date=2022-10-26 |website=hoopsforkids |language=en}} He remains passionate about philanthropy and giving back to the community.
